paragraphs: Friend, this whole song is love out loud. Two people, and neither one is shy about it. She says his love is "more delightful than wine," and he tells her, "How beautiful you are, my darling! Oh, how very beautiful!" (Song of Solomon 1:2, 1:15). It's a song, and God put it in His Book, so I figure He thinks delighted, honest love is worth singing about.

Now look at how she shows up. She's dark from the sun, her own vineyard is neglected, and she still says, "I am dark, yet lovely" (Song of Solomon 1:5-6). I think that's brave, friend. And the one who loves her doesn't fix her up first. He calls her "a lily among the thorns" (Song of Solomon 2:2). Real love sees you the way you are and says you're lovely, and I'm still getting used to being seen like that myself.

Then comes the line that holds it all together: "Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right" (Song of Solomon 2:7). Love is a gift, and good gifts come in their own time, so you don't rush it. Pull it out early and you've got a tray of GOO. So wait, baker, trust the timing, and know that this story isn't over, because the song keeps going.
